hits.name: Sahil Bloom
hits.text: The older I get, the more I realize you can get pretty damn far in life by just doing what most people avoid. Wake up early. Focus deeply. Move your body. Eat real foods. Obsess over one thing. Have difficult conversations. Slow down. Be present. It’s the recipe for a good life.
hits.full_text: The older I get, the more I realize you can get pretty damn far in life by just doing what most people avoid. Wake up early. Focus deeply. Move your body. Eat real foods. Obsess over one thing. Have difficult conversations. Slow down. Be present. It’s the recipe for a good life.
hits.hook: SahilBloom — do what most people avoid
hits.draft_en:
I keep noticing that the useful days aren't the ones where I invent a new system.

They're the ones where I do the small thing I usually skip.

One honest page. The pen I actually like. A quiet ten minutes before I open anything else.

Nothing clever. Just not avoiding the part that works.
hits.video_tip: 20–30s desk: phone face-down → uncap Montblanc / favorite pen → write one plain line. VO: 'The useful days aren't new systems. They're the small thing I usually skip.'
